TIJCEF Completes STEM Empowerment Project, Reaches 400 Girls in Yola

TIJCEF Completes STEM Empowerment Project, Reaches 400 Girls in Yola

 

Tijwun Care and Empowerment Foundation (TIJCEF) successfully completed its STEM Empowerment Project on 23 February 2026 at Government Girls’ School, Yola, Adamawa State. The completed intervention reached 400 girls and strengthened their exposure to science, technology, engineering and mathematics as pathways to education, innovation, leadership and future economic opportunities.

 

The project was implemented under TIJCEF’s Agency Pillar, which focuses on enabling women and girls to develop the knowledge, confidence, skills and opportunities required to make informed choices and shape their own futures.

 

Rather than viewing the participating students only as beneficiaries, the initiative recognised them as individuals with ideas, ambitions and the capacity to contribute meaningfully to their communities. It encouraged the girls to see themselves as potential scientists, engineers, healthcare professionals, surveyors, researchers, environmental specialists, technology entrepreneurs and leaders.

 

Building Agency Through STEM Education

 

For TIJCEF, agency means more than giving assistance to women and girls. It involves creating opportunities that allow them to recognise their abilities, express their ideas, make informed decisions and pursue their aspirations without being restricted by gender stereotypes or limited exposure.

 

The STEM Empowerment Project reflected this commitment by introducing 400 girls to the possibilities available within science and technology-related fields. It was designed to strengthen their confidence and encourage them to approach STEM subjects as areas in which they could participate, grow and succeed.

 

Science, technology, engineering and mathematics are not simply academic subjects. They help young people develop curiosity, creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. These skills can support girls in making better decisions, responding to challenges and developing solutions that benefit their schools, families and communities.

 

By bringing the intervention directly to Government Girls’ School, Yola, TIJCEF created an opportunity to engage the students within their learning environment. Schools are important spaces for building agency because the encouragement girls receive during their formative years can influence their educational choices, professional ambitions and willingness to take on leadership responsibilities.

 

Helping Girls See New Possibilities

 

Many girls have the ability to succeed in STEM but may not always receive the exposure, encouragement or opportunities needed to develop their interests. Social expectations and gender stereotypes can sometimes create the impression that technical and scientific fields are more suitable for boys.

 

Limited access to role models and relevant learning opportunities can also affect how girls perceive their abilities and available career options. When these barriers are not addressed, talented girls may abandon their interests or avoid subjects and professions they are fully capable of pursuing.

 

TIJCEF’s STEM Empowerment Project helped challenge these limitations by encouraging the participating girls to recognise that their gender does not determine their intelligence, potential or professional future.

 

The initiative promoted a simple but important message: girls have the right and ability to learn, innovate, lead and contribute to technological and scientific development.

 

This message is central to the Agency Pillar. A girl who believes in her ability to learn is more likely to ask questions, explore opportunities and make informed decisions about her education. She is also better positioned to resist limiting stereotypes and pursue a future based on her interests and abilities.

 

From Beneficiaries to Future Problem-Solvers

 

TIJCEF believes that girls should not only receive support but should also be equipped to become active problem-solvers and decision-makers.

 

The 400 girls reached through the completed project represent 400 individual ambitions with the potential to influence families, communities and institutions. Each participant has the capacity to use knowledge and confidence gained through educational opportunities to contribute to society.

 

A girl encouraged to pursue STEM today may become an engineer who designs essential infrastructure, a healthcare professional who improves community wellbeing, a researcher who generates new evidence, a surveyor who supports sustainable development or a technology entrepreneur who creates jobs.

 

Others may apply STEM-related skills to agriculture, climate action, education, communication or environmental management. The ultimate value of STEM empowerment is not limited to the number of girls reached; it is also reflected in the choices they become confident enough to make and the solutions they may create in the future.

 

A Completed Project with Lasting Significance

 

Although the STEM Empowerment Project was completed on 23 February 2026, its significance extends beyond the completion date. The encouragement, exposure and sense of possibility created through the initiative can continue to influence the participants as they progress through their education.

 

Project completion represents the achievement of a defined intervention, but it does not end TIJCEF’s commitment to promoting girls’ education and leadership. Instead, it provides a foundation for strengthening future initiatives and reaching more girls in other schools and communities.

 

The completion of the project also demonstrates TIJCEF’s commitment to implementing practical interventions with clearly identified beneficiaries, locations and outcomes. Reaching 400 girls at Government Girls’ School, Yola, represents a measurable contribution to the Foundation’s broader goal of expanding opportunities for women and girls.

 

Investing in Girls’ Agency

 

Investing in girls’ agency benefits entire communities. Girls who are educated, confident and empowered to make informed decisions are better positioned to participate in leadership, innovation and economic development.

 

As technology continues to transform education, healthcare, agriculture, environmental management and employment, girls must be prepared to participate not only as users of technology but also as creators, researchers and decision-makers.

 

The completed STEM Empowerment Project at Government Girls’ School, Yola, reflects TIJCEF’s determination to ensure that girls are not left behind. By reaching 400 students, the Foundation created an opportunity for the participants to see STEM as accessible and their ambitions as achievable.

 

The project stands as an important milestone under TIJCEF’s Agency Pillar. It demonstrates how targeted educational interventions can strengthen girls’ confidence, expand their awareness of future opportunities and encourage them to take greater ownership of their educational and professional journeys.

 

Through initiatives of this nature, TIJCEF continues to advance a future in which women and girls have the knowledge, voice, confidence and opportunities required to make choices, pursue their aspirations and contribute meaningfully to society.

 

Project status: Completed

Completion date: 23 February 2026

Beneficiaries reached: 400 girls

Location: Government Girls’ School, Yola, Adamawa State

TIJCEF pillar: Agency
